questions.stem: This contrast-enhanced axial CT of the chest shows red arrows pointing to filling defects within the central pulmonary arteries. What is the most likely diagnosis?

explanation.summary: On CT pulmonary angiography, hypodense (dark) filling defects within the contrast-opacified pulmonary arteries indicate thromboemboli. Large central emboli can cause hyperventilation and a secondary respiratory alkalosis.
explanation.whyCorrect: On CT pulmonary angiography, hypodense (dark) filling defects within the contrast-opacified pulmonary arteries indicate thromboemboli. Large central emboli can cause hyperventilation and a secondary respiratory alkalosis.
